slides.0.title: Other European Grape Spirits
slides.0.subtitle: Brandy de Jerez, Metaxa, Deutscher Weinbrand and Grappa
slides.1.title: Brandy de Jerez
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The solera system
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Aged by criaderas y soleras, in 500-litre American oak casks that held sherry, the sherry type shaping flavour (Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Three categories
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Solera at least 6 months on average; Solera Reserva at least 1 year; Solera Gran Reserva at least 3 years (Wikipedia citing the Consejo Regulador)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Holandas
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Low-strength pot-still spirits, seen as higher quality, must make up at least 50% of the final brandy; high-strength column spirit at most 50%
slides.1.content: Jerez's round sweetness comes from sherry casks and long solera blending.
slides.2.title: Metaxa and Deutscher Weinbrand
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Metaxa
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Founded in 1888 by Spyros Metaxa; a blend of distillate with Samos Muscat wine and Mediterranean botanicals including May rose. Once labelled Cognac, then brandy, until naming rules forbade it (Wikipedia); a flavoured "Greek spirit" rather than a standard brandy
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Deutscher Weinbrand
slides.2.highlights.1.content: A German PGI: at least 38% abv, at least 12 months in oak under 1,000 L, at least 85% of the distillate distilled in Germany, sugar at most 20 g/L and no caramel colouring (EU GI file)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Asbach
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Asbach Uralt is a well-known German Weinbrand brand
slides.2.content: German base wine need not come from German grapes, unlike Cognac's place-bound rules.
slides.3.title: Grappa
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Made from pomace
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Grappa is distilled from the skins, seeds and stems left after winemaking (pomace, or marc), so it is a marc spirit rather than a wine brandy
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Strength
slides.3.highlights.1.content: At least 37.5% in general; with a regional name (such as Grappa di Barolo) at least 40% (Difford's Guide)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Ageing terms
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Vecchia or Invecchiata means at least 12 months in wood; Riserva or Stravecchia at least 18 months; a named single variety must be at least 85%
slides.3.content: Note: in the EU grappa is a grape marc spirit, a separate category from brandy.
